# Defence-in-depth parity matrix

Which Constitution rules a tool actually blocks, and which rely on review.

This file is generated from the `enforcement` field of each rule in `rules/constitution.ts`, so
it cannot overclaim: to make a row say **Yes**, you have to make the rule actually blocking.
That matters, because the hand-written claim this replaces ("a hook (ESLint) enforces #1, #2,
#5") was wrong about all three — there was no hook, #1 was scoped to spec files only, and #2
was a non-blocking warning.

**13 of 15 rules are mechanically blocking today.**

| Rule | Forbidden                                                                     | Mechanism                                                                                                                                               | Blocks the build? | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| #1   | `page.waitForTimeout(...)`                                                    | ESLint `playwright/no-wait-for-timeout (+ no-restricted-syntax)` (tests/**, pages/**, helpers/**, fixtures/**)                                          | **Yes**           | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| #2   | `page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` on an SPA                              | ESLint `playwright/no-networkidle` (tests/**, pages/**, helpers/**, fixtures/**)                                                                        | **Yes**           | Severity is 'warn', but `npm run lint` passes --max-warnings=0, so it fails the build. Kept as a warning so a genuine static/SSR use can be justified with an inline disable directive rather than being impossible.                                                                                               |

| #6   | `z.object(...)` for an API schema                                             | ESLint `no-restricted-syntax (bare z.object as a schema value)` (fixtures/**, test-data/**, helpers/\*\*)                                               | **Yes**           | Deliberately does NOT flag `z.object(...).catchall(z.unknown())` — that chain is the explicit opt-in to a permissive schema, which a Salesforce describe payload legitimately needs.                                                                                                                               |
| #7   | Skipping `expect(Schema.parse(body))` / `{ schema }` on an API response       | TypeScript (compile error)                                                                                                                              | **Yes**           | `ApiRequest`'s overloads derive the result type from the schema. Without a schema `data` is `unknown`, so the compiler refuses any field access on it — an unvalidated response can no longer masquerade as typed. Legitimately body-less calls (204, status-only, teardown) never touch `data` and still compile. |

## How to read this

- **Blocks the build** means a violation fails `npm run lint` (or the guard script) and
  therefore fails the CI `quality` job. Anything else is caught by a human, or not at all.
- **Enforced more narrowly than it is declared.** These rules are blocking, but the lint
  scope misses directories the rule itself claims to cover — a violation there ships:
  - rule #11 — not checked in `pages/`, `helpers/`, `test-data/`
- Review-only is a legitimate answer for rule #4 (A guessed selector, URL, enum value, endpoint, or UI string) and rule #15 (A Salesforce object or field API name written from memory) — that is a question about
  process, not syntax, and no linter can see it.
